slides.title: Patterns in Mathematics
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome students. Mathematics is more than arithmetic — it's the search for patterns.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Spot the rule of a number sequence and find the next term.
Recognise common sequences: counting, even, odd, square, triangular, cube, Fibonacci.
Draw dot diagrams for square and triangular numbers.
Connect number patterns and shape patterns.
slides.speaker_notes: Read each; ask which seems hardest.

slides.title: What is mathematics?
bullets: Not just numbers — the search for PATTERNS.
Patterns are everywhere — petals, bricks, sound waves.
slides.speaker_notes: Set the spirit of the chapter.

slides.title: Famous number sequences
slides.speaker_notes: List on board with one example computed each.

slides.title: More sequences worth knowing
bullets: Each has a clear rule — once you spot it, you can extend forever.
slides.speaker_notes: Fibonacci appears in pine cones and flower petals.

slides.title: Find the rule, find the next term
slides.speaker_notes: Two ways of seeing the same pattern.

slides.title: Visualising — square numbers
bullets: Why 'square'? Because the dots form a SQUARE.
slides.speaker_notes: Have students draw 4 × 4 in their notebooks.

slides.title: Visualising — triangular numbers
bullets: Why 'triangular'? The dots form a TRIANGLE.
slides.speaker_notes: Triangular numbers appear in stacked logs and bowling pins.

slides.title: Surprise! Sum of odd numbers = square
slides.speaker_notes: Draw the L-shape strips inside a 4×4 grid to PROVE this visually.

slides.title: The famous formula: triangular(n) = n(n+1)/2
bullets: Two copies of an n-row triangle fit into an n × (n+1) rectangle.
Number of dots in the rectangle = n × (n + 1).
Each triangle has half the dots: n × (n + 1) / 2.
slides.speaker_notes: Tell the Gauss anecdote — child mathematician summed 1 to 100 in seconds.

slides.title: Two consecutive triangulars sum to a square
bullets: Picture: two triangles stack into a square.
slides.speaker_notes: Beautiful pattern — relates two famous sequences.

slides.title: Patterns in shapes
bullets: Every shape sequence has a number rule.
slides.speaker_notes: Shapes give a 'WHY' that pure numbers sometimes hide.

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 4. Find triangular(5) + triangular(6) — is it a square?
5. Make up a sequence with rule 'add 6 each time, starting at 4'.
slides.speaker_notes: Walk the room; address common slips.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q4. Sum of first 7 odd numbers?
slides.speaker_notes: Address the question with the most disagreement.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Common sequences: counting / even / odd / square / triangular / cube / Fibonacci / powers.
Sum of first n odd numbers = n^2.
Two consecutive triangulars sum to a square.
Switch between numbers and shapes when stuck.
slides.speaker_notes: Hand out the worksheet; announce homework.
